problems.note: The replication does not report a participant-level submission-depth outcome or this fluency-specific contrast. Table 2 reports registered designers, participating designers, and aggregate submissions by arm. The general statement about participation does not identify submission depth; the cited Web Appendix D.1 and Table WA-D.1 concern designer attributes (reputation, past-project quality, professionalism, hire-again ratings, jobs, reviews, and hourly rate), with no submission-depth row. The participant counts themselves are correct, but they do not establish an analysis of this outcome. Rule 4 requires a contrast reported by the paper. Retain the Table 2 counts as sample information; remove this unsupported estimate unless an outcome-specific result can be sourced. Do not derive arm means by dividing aggregate submissions by participants under rule 1.

summary: Read the complete markdown conversion, including all appendices, and checked all 27 estimates against the PDF. All recorded numerical statistics and participant counts match their cited pages and columns. Two replication records assert participant-level submission-depth contrasts that could not be found; the replication supplies participant/output totals and a general participation statement, not a fluency-specific result. The other 25 retained records are supported. Appendix E arm membership and analysis counts remain unresolved in the paper and are appropriately qualified or null. The main quality and originality regressions are correctly excluded under rule 5 because they adjust for post-assignment submission date; the quality-selected subsets are not full-sample contrasts. No additional eligible full-sample outcome or contrast was found.
